summary: Defines a YANG data model for configuring and managing IGMP and MLD proxy devices. It conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture.

eli5.summary: A standard settings form for devices that pass along group-membership requests for multicast streams.

questions: how to manage igmp proxy devices
subtitle: Standard configuration model for multicast proxy devices.

tldr.problem: Network operators need a standard way to configure and manage IGMP and MLD proxy devices that forward group membership requests across networks.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9398 defines a YANG data model that augments the standard routing management model, allowing operators to configure upstream interfaces for IGMP (IPv4) and MLD (IPv6) proxies, and retrieve operational state.
tldr.outcome: Organizations can manage multicast proxy forwarding consistently using standard network management protocols like NETCONF and RESTCONF.

today: RFC 9398 is an Internet Standard and remains the current data model for managing IGMP/MLD proxy devices.

sections.title: What Is a Multicast Proxy
sections.content:
Multicast is a way to send data to many receivers at once without sending separate copies to each one. Networks use IGMP (for IPv4) and MLD (for IPv6) to let devices join multicast groups and request data. A proxy is a device that forwards these membership requests from one part of a network to another, bridging networks where direct multicast routing is not available.

This RFC defines a YANG data model for configuring and managing these proxy devices. YANG is a standard language for network configuration that lets administrators manage devices consistently across different vendors using standard management protocols like NETCONF and RESTCONF.
sections.eli5: A proxy device passes along membership requests from one side of a network to the other, kind of like a post office forwarding mail. This is a standard settings form so all post offices work the same way.

sections.title: Design Goals
sections.content:
The data model is designed to represent the core capabilities of IGMP/MLD Proxy devices that implementations from multiple vendors can support. The RFC conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA), which separates configuration data from operational state in a standard way.

The model separates IPv4 IGMP proxy and IPv6 MLD proxy into distinct branches. This separation allows implementations to support IGMP proxies, MLD proxies, or both independently, and cleanly models differences between the two protocols.
sections.eli5: The design lets different brands build their own proxy devices but all use the same settings form. It separates the IPv4 and IPv6 settings into different sections because they work a bit differently.

sections.title: Module Structure and Integration
sections.content:
The YANG module augments the core routing data model defined in RFC 8349. An augment in YANG adds new data to an existing model without modifying the original. The model adds an igmp-proxy container for IPv4 and an mld-proxy container for IPv6, each containing configuration and operational state for upstream interfaces.

Each container holds a list of upstream interfaces. For IGMP proxies, these are IPv4 interfaces where the device listens for membership requests. For MLD proxies, these are IPv6 interfaces. The module also requires that upstream interfaces cannot be configured to use PIM (Protocol Independent Multicast), which is a different multicast routing protocol.
sections.eli5: The settings form plugs into a standard routing settings form. It adds sections for the upstream interfaces where the device listens for membership requests, and makes sure these interfaces don't accidentally use a different multicast method.

sections.title: Configuration and State Parameters
sections.content:
For each upstream interface, the model allows configuration of:

  • Protocol version: IGMP version (1, 2, or 3, default 2) or MLD version (1 or 2, default 2)
  • Enabled: A boolean to turn the proxy on or off
  • Sender source address: Optional IPv4 or IPv6 address used when sending membership reports

Downstream interfaces, where the proxy sends requests to receivers, are configured using the standard IGMP/MLD data model in RFC 8652. The operational state shows the multicast groups currently being proxied, the sources sending to each group, and which downstream interfaces are receiving traffic for each source.
sections.eli5: The settings let you pick which version of the multicast protocol to use, turn the proxy on or off, and optionally set a source address to use when asking for traffic. The device automatically tracks which channels are being requested and where to send them.

sections.title: Security and Access Control
sections.content:
Since this model configures network forwarding behavior, improper access could misroute multicast traffic. The RFC recommends using NETCONF over SSH or RESTCONF over HTTPS with TLS for secure transport. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) can restrict access to sensitive configuration and state data.

The writable subtrees under igmp-proxy and mld-proxy are sensitive because modifying them can cause proxy interfaces to be deleted or changed, affecting multicast delivery. The readable operational state (group memberships and source information) is also sensitive because it reveals which multicast groups are active on the network.
sections.eli5: Only trusted network managers should be allowed to change these settings, since mistakes could break multicast TV or other group services. The settings should be accessed over secure encrypted connections.

sections.title: The Model Today
sections.content: RFC 9398 is an Internet Standard published in May 2023. It is actively used by vendors implementing IGMP/MLD proxy management. Organizations deploying multicast proxies can use this standard YANG model to manage these devices consistently alongside other YANG-based network management.
sections.eli5: This is the official standard settings form for multicast proxy devices and is ready for use today.
